questions: When the board is fully in view, are there exactly three pens on it (no missing pen and no empty gap)?
Do all three pens point the same direction, with none flipped or reversed relative to the other two?
Are all three pens the same color as each other, with none differing in color?
Is every pen complete and capped, with none showing a bare/exposed writing tip or looking clearly shorter than the others?
Does the board move smoothly and continuously from left to right, without stopping, freezing, pausing, reversing, or jamming at any point?

question_answers.evidence: When the board is fully in view (e.g., 00:06-00:10), there are exactly three pens visible on the white board.
All three pens appear to be oriented with the black capped end pointing downwards and the translucent barrel upwards. None are flipped relative to the others in terms of up/down direction.
All three pens appear to be the same color (black caps, translucent barrels with dark ink).
The middle pen appears clearly shorter than the left and right pens (visible from 00:06 onwards), suggesting it is missing its cap or is a different/shorter pen, breaking the uniformity.
The board moves smoothly and continuously from left to right throughout the video without stopping or jamming.

parsed.reason: The middle pen is visibly shorter than the other two identical pens, which indicates a missing cap or a defect in length, violating the condition that all pens must be identical and complete.

description: Temporal/motion anomaly in the board movement.
